html:
The Westgate shopping mall attack began on 21 September 2013, when gunmen of al-Shabaab stormed an upscale mall in Nairobi, Kenya, killing 67 people in a siege that lasted four days.

The Somali group said it was punishing Kenya for sending troops into Somalia in 2011. The gunmen singled out non-Muslims, and the security response was chaotic, with soldiers accused of looting the mall.

It was followed by other attacks, among them the killing of 148 people, mostly students, at Garissa University in 2015. The attacks brought harsh crackdowns on Somali and Muslim communities in Kenya, and showed the reach of al-Shabaab beyond Somalia.
sum: The Westgate shopping mall attack began on 21 September 2013, when gunmen of al-Shabaab stormed an upscale mall in Nairobi, Kenya, killing 67 people in a siege that lasted four days.
